note: Second half of the literature lens, same method as literature-01: every claim searched against the 1,376-record screened corpus with build/lit/corpus_search.py, and every locator below is a record that exists in documentation/refs/systematic/records.jsonl.

opinions.rationale: The framing is now published rather than a preprint: the ideal-trial paper the entry cites as arXiv 2405.10026 appeared in Epidemiology in 2026, and the entry should cite the journal version. A 2026 American Journal of Epidemiology paper sets out the anatomy of a causal estimand for population health research, which is the vocabulary a lineage would be written in. Neither supplies the decomposition the entry asks for: a formal accounting that attributes total discrepancy across the four transitions, with a computable measure of estimand distance. The claim survives with its citation corrected and its neighbors named.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: The distinction between ideal, target and emulated trials is established and published; no decomposition attributes a study's total discrepancy across scientific-target mismatch, protocol compromise, observational mapping and estimation, and no computable measure of estimand distance is in use.

resolving_work.title: The ideal trial: defining causal estimands that balance relevance and feasibility in target trial emulations and actual randomized trials
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: The peer-reviewed version of the framing the entry cites as a preprint. The entry's citation should move to this.

resolving_work.title: Clarifying causal questions in population health research: anatomy of a causal estimand
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Decomposes a causal estimand into its parts, which is the representation an estimand lineage would build on.

opinions.rationale: The entry says standard inference conditions on a fixed target trial and ignores the search over candidate emulations. The search is now being reported in at least one applied setting: a 2025 European Journal of Epidemiology study uses a multiverse analysis to characterize uncertainty in the estimated effect of statin initiation on dementia across design choices. That is the design multiverse the entry proposes, already run. What remains unaddressed is the inferential half: a multiverse displays the spread and does not correct coverage, and no selective-inference treatment of protocol selection exists in the corpus. The entry should not claim the multiverse is absent.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: Design multiverse analyses of emulations exist and display the spread of estimates across specifications; no correction restores coverage for the search that produced the reported specification, and no registration format records rejected alternatives.

resolving_work.title: Uncertainty in the estimated effects of statin initiation on risk of dementia: using a multiverse analysis
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Runs the design multiverse the entry proposes, in an applied emulation, which means the proposal has a precedent rather than being untried.

resolving_work.title: Emulations of oncology trials using real-world data: a systematic literature review
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Documents the specification choices oncology emulations actually make, which is the empirical base for describing the search space.

opinions.rationale: Nothing in the corpus records a decision log, a dated chronology of design choices, or the alternatives rejected during protocol development. Quality-assessment tools for observational comparative effectiveness studies, and comprehensive analyses of emulation practice in oncology, evaluate the specification that was published rather than the process that produced it. The entry's claim is about an artifact nobody keeps, which is consistent with its absence from a literature search: the evidence for it is the absence of any paper reporting one.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: No published emulation reports a dated decision log or the protocol versions it rejected, and appraisal instruments evaluate the final specification only.

resolving_work.title: Methodological quality assessment tool for observational studies comparing treatment effectiveness in infectious diseases
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: An appraisal instrument for exactly these studies, which assesses the reported design and not the chronology by which it was reached.

opinions.rationale: Operational frameworks for mapping each protocol component onto record data exist, and a 2024 Frontiers in Pharmacology case study applies the estimand and target trial frameworks together to an external control analysis, which is the closest the corpus comes to naming the substituted estimand explicitly. None requires that the substituted estimand replace the intended one in the paper's headline, and none supplies criteria for which substitutions preserve the question. The entry's claim is about a reporting requirement rather than a method, and no such requirement appears in the reporting literature.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: When a protocol component cannot be realized in the data, no reporting convention requires the resulting data-defined estimand to be stated in place of the intended one, and no criteria distinguish innocuous substitutions from ones that change the question.

resolving_work.title: Applying the estimand and target trial frameworks to external control analyses using observational data: a case study
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Combines the estimand framework with the target trial framework so the realized estimand is stated, which is the practice the entry asks to be made general.

resolving_work.title: An operational target trial emulation framework for causal inference using electronic health records
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Works through the operational realization of each component, which is where substitutions occur.

opinions.rationale: The corpus contains policy and service-level emulations, including chronic disease management programs and national incentive schemes evaluated with the target trial approach, and contains no protocol template stating which components a policy intervention can satisfy or what estimand results when several cannot. A 2026 substance-use workshop proceedings discusses methodological innovation for emulation in that setting, which is the nearest thing to the templates the entry asks for. The claim that policy emulations are published with individual-level precision and jurisdiction-level information is supported by the applied papers in the corpus rather than by a methodological source, which is why the confidence is moderate.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: No protocol template states which of the seven components a cluster-assigned or policy intervention can satisfy, or what estimand results when the treatment version varies by implementer.

resolving_work.title: Methodological innovations to advance substance use disorder research: proceedings of a NIDA workshop on target trial emulation
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Addresses emulation in a service and policy setting where the intervention is delivered at more than the individual level.

opinions.rationale: Nothing in the corpus defines a network target trial with an explicit exposure mapping, cluster-level clone-censor-weighting, or a positivity condition stated for joint neighborhood exposure. The interference literature is present in the corpus only through its own methodological line, and the multi-site and distributed-analysis papers address data governance rather than interference. The claim that individual cloning can assign clones a joint strategy no cluster could receive is a structural argument the entry makes rather than one the corpus states, and it follows from the definitions.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: Emulation protocols assume no interference, and no cluster or network extension of the emulation protocol, of clone-censor-weighting, or of the positivity condition has been published.

opinions.rationale: Transport methods are reaching emulation practice faster than the entry allows. A 2026 Clinical Pharmacology and Therapeutics paper performs post hoc population standardization of trial emulation studies in claims data within RCT-DUPLICATE, which is transport applied to the benchmarking corpus itself. Nurse home visiting was emulated in the policy-relevant population using targeted learning and transport, and the scoping review the entry cites documents the practice broadly. What survives is the compounding claim: no reporting practice shows how sampling exchangeability and treatment exchangeability compound, or which of the two a discrepancy should be charged to.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: Transport estimators are being applied to emulations, including within benchmarking programs; nothing shows how the sampling-exchangeability and treatment-exchangeability assumptions compound, or attributes a transported estimate's error between them.

resolving_work.title: Post hoc population standardization of trial emulation studies in claims data: an RCT-DUPLICATE analysis
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Standardizes emulations to trial populations inside the largest benchmarking program, which is transport applied where the entry says it is underused.

resolving_work.title: Emulating a target trial of intensive nurse home visiting in the policy-relevant population using linked administrative data
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Combines the target trial framework with transport and targeted learning to reach a policy-relevant population.

opinions.rationale: The estimand vocabulary is arriving in the emulation literature: a 2026 Trials paper applies a hypothetical strategy to the intercurrent event of non-adherence using the parametric g-formula, which is the ICH E9(R1) discipline executed inside a longitudinal analysis, and a 2026 Journal of Epidemiology paper argues explicitly for going beyond the hazard ratio when censoring, confounding and competing events are present. The entry's claim is about what published reports lead with rather than what is possible, and no reporting requirement in the corpus mandates a one-sentence estimand statement or absolute-risk reporting. The presence of these papers means the entry should not imply the vocabulary is missing.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: Estimand vocabulary and absolute-risk alternatives are available and are being used in methodological work; no reporting standard requires an emulation to state its estimand in one sentence or to lead with an absolute measure, and hazard ratios remain the headline.

resolving_work.title: Applying a hypothetical strategy to the intercurrent event of non-adherence with the parametric g-formula
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Executes an ICH E9(R1) intercurrent-event strategy inside a g-formula analysis, which is the alignment the entry asks for.

resolving_work.title: Beyond the hazard ratio: causal inference from time-to-event data with dependent censoring, confounding, and competing events
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Argues directly against the hazard ratio as the reported quantity in this setting.

opinions.rationale: The entry treats comparator convergence as an unhandled feature of the observational intention-to-treat analogue. Treatment switching is a well-developed area with its own methods and its own scoping review. A 2025 Clinical Pharmacology and Therapeutics scoping review catalogs statistical methods to adjust for treatment switching in real-world studies and offers a decision framework for choosing among them. A 2026 American Journal of Epidemiology paper warns specifically about how switchers are handled in pharmacoepidemiologic effect estimation, and a 2024 BMC Medical Research Methodology paper applies g-methods to switching in the ALTA-1L trial. The entry's implicit claim that the analyst has no options is wrong. What survives is narrower and still real: reporting the cumulative incidence of initiation in both arms is not conventional, so a reader cannot see how far the strategies stayed distinct, and no convention exists for choosing the horizon at which the contrast remains meaningful.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: Methods for handling treatment switching exist and have been reviewed; emulations do not conventionally report initiation trajectories in both arms, so a reader cannot judge how far the contrasted strategies remained distinct over follow-up.

resolving_work.title: Statistical methods to adjust for treatment switching in real-world clinical studies: a scoping review and decision framework
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Catalogs the available methods and supplies a framework for choosing among them, which contradicts the entry's implication that convergence cannot be addressed.

resolving_work.title: Caution in handling switchers in pharmacoepidemiologic studies estimating treatment effects
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Addresses the specific analytic hazard of switchers in effect estimation.

resolving_work.title: Addressing treatment switching in the ALTA-1L trial with g-methods: exploring the impact of model specification
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Applies g-methods to switching and examines the sensitivity of the result to specification.

opinions.rationale: The entry says data-fitness assessment is narrative with no quantitative thresholds. A 2026 JAMIA Open paper assesses the quality of electronic health record data and linked claims data specifically for target trial emulation studies, which is a quantitative fitness assessment for this purpose and not a narrative one. Regulatory syntheses for GLP-1 therapies and oncology reviews also set out data-adequacy considerations. What none supplies is the predefined stop rule the entry asks for, or the publication of a negative fitness assessment as a citable result, so the operational half of the claim stands and the descriptive half is too strong.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: Data-quality assessment for emulation exists and is being formalized; no predefined stop rule exists that would halt a study when an essential protocol component fails, and a negative fitness assessment is not a publishable result.

resolving_work.title: Assessing the quality of electronic health record data and the claims linked data for target trial emulation studies
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Assesses data quality for the emulation purpose specifically, which is the fitness assessment the entry says does not exist quantitatively.

resolving_work.title: Methodological approaches to real-world evidence generation for GLP-1-based therapies: a synopsis
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Sets out data-adequacy considerations for a high-stakes therapeutic area where emulation is being used for decisions.

opinions.rationale: Federated emulation has advanced past the feasibility demonstration the entry cites. POLARIS supplies a one-shot likelihood approach for federated emulation with time-to-event outcomes that claims pooled-equivalent estimates, and a 2026 JAMIA paper sets out ten principles for high-quality multi-site studies using privacy-preserving distributed algorithms, which is directly the site-validation discipline the entry asks for. The entry's specific claim, that averaging site estimates can conceal that sites emulated different trials and that nothing in the aggregation detects it, is not answered by either: both improve the statistics of pooling rather than detecting semantic incompatibility.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: Federated estimation for emulated trials is developed and its governance is being codified; no diagnostic detects that sites operationalized the same protocol into materially different eligibility, exposure or outcome definitions, and heterogeneity statistics cannot separate that from real effect modification.

resolving_work.title: Federated target trial emulation for time-to-event outcomes via POLARIS
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Provides pooled-equivalent federated estimation for emulated trials with survival outcomes, well past feasibility.

resolving_work.title: Privacy-preserving distributed algorithms in action: ten principles for high-quality multi-site clinical studies
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Codifies multi-site conduct including site-level validation, which is the gate the entry proposes.

opinions.rationale: A search for linkage or common-data-model work addressing semantic drift, provenance graphs or phenotype invariance returned nothing in the screened corpus. The concordance meta-analysis provides indirect support by finding that claims-based emulations tended to underestimate trial effects and that outcome-emulation quality predicted agreement, which is the data-provenance channel operating without being measured directly. The absence is the evidence here, so the confidence is capped: informatics venues indexed outside these eight phrases would not have been retrieved.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: No published emulation carries a provenance record from source field to analytic variable, and no diagnostic tests phenotype invariance across extracts or code-system versions, although data source and outcome-emulation quality are known to predict agreement with trials.

opinions.rationale: The entry proposes prospective, blinded benchmarking in which the protocol is frozen before the trial reports. That design now has at least one instance: a 2026 Circulation paper emulates a reference trial to predict the results of COBRRA before the trial's result was available. So the proposal is not untried and the entry should say so. The theoretical claim survives intact: nothing licenses the inference from a successful replication in one database to a new question or a new database, and the concordance meta-analysis reports determinants of emulation success without supplying that extrapolation. One correction the entry must carry: the meta-analysis it cites has a published erratum, so any figure quoted from it needs checking against the corrected version. Supporting quotation retained here rather than as counter-evidence: [10.1136/bmj-2026-100303] Published Erratum to the concordance systematic review and meta-analysis. Any figure the entry quotes from that paper must be checked against the corrected version before publication.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: Prospective blinded emulation of a pending trial has been done at least once; no theory licenses extrapolating a successful replication to a new question or data source, and the benchmarking corpus is a selected sample of favorable questions.

resolving_work.title: Bleeding risk with apixaban versus rivaroxaban: a reference trial emulation predicting the results of COBRRA
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: A prospective emulation issued as a prediction of a trial's result, which is the blinded benchmarking design the entry proposes as future work.

resolving_work.title: Concordance between target trial emulation and randomised controlled trials: systematic review and meta-analysis
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Supplies the concordance estimates and their determinants across paired emulations and trials.

opinions.rationale: The entry criticizes binary replication labels. The concordance meta-analysis it draws on does not use one: it reports correlation and standardized-difference agreement and relates them to design features, which is the graded reporting the entry asks for. RCT-DUPLICATE similarly reports several agreement metrics. So the criticism lands on the citing practice rather than on the benchmarking literature, and the entry should say that. The part that survives is that a graded criterion still does not separate estimand mismatch from random error, since prediction-interval coverage requires a distributional claim about the trial's own error that trials do not publish.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: Benchmarking programs report graded agreement measures; the downstream literature cites them as pass or fail, and no reported measure separates estimand mismatch from random error.

resolving_work.title: Emulation of randomized clinical trials with nonrandomized database analyses: results of 32 clinical trials
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Reports multiple agreement metrics rather than a single binary label.

resolving_work.title: Concordance between target trial emulation and randomised controlled trials: systematic review and meta-analysis
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Reports correlation and standardized agreement and relates both to design features, which is graded rather than binary.

opinions.rationale: The corpus contains regulatory and decision-facing syntheses for oncology, cardiology devices and GLP-1 therapies, all of which describe considerations rather than thresholds. A 2026 Journal of Clinical Oncology paper addresses emulation for regulatory and clinical decision making in cancer without setting an acceptance criterion. This is consistent with the entry: guidance exists, thresholds do not, and the reason given by the entry, that the quantities that would be thresholded are not identified from the study's own data, is a structural reason rather than an oversight.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: Regulatory and health technology assessment guidance names emulation as an acceptable approach and sets no threshold for adequate emulation, acceptable residual confounding or sufficient sensitivity analysis.

resolving_work.title: Target trial emulation for regulatory and clinical decision making in cancer
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Addresses the decision-facing use of emulation directly, and describes considerations rather than acceptance thresholds.

opinions.rationale: No assumption dashboard appears in the corpus. Methodological quality assessment tools for observational comparative effectiveness studies exist and score reported design features rather than requiring a standard diagnostic panel, and none separates empirically testable diagnostics from untestable assumptions in its output. The entry's claim that a missing diagnostic cannot be distinguished from an unreported one follows from the absence of a required panel and is supported by the reporting review showing that 43% of 200 emulations did not describe all key components.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: No standard diagnostic panel exists for an emulation, so an unreported diagnostic and an unrun one look identical, and no reporting instrument separates testable diagnostics from untestable assumptions.

resolving_work.title: Methodological quality assessment tool for observational studies comparing treatment effectiveness in infectious diseases
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: An appraisal instrument in this space, which scores what was reported rather than requiring a diagnostic panel.

resolving_work.title: Reporting of observational studies explicitly aiming to emulate randomized trials: a systematic review
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Measures how incompletely emulations report their components, which is the baseline the entry's claim rests on.

opinions.rationale: The corpus shows the label spreading rapidly across clinical specialties, with comprehensive analyses of emulation practice in oncology and reviews in neurology, multiple sclerosis and military medicine, and it contains no published ladder of assumption levels with named rungs, and no study stating which rung its evidence reaches. The reporting review's finding that 43% of studies claiming to emulate a trial did not describe all key components is direct evidence that the label constrains practice weakly, which is the entry's central claim.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: No published scheme names the rungs of the assumption ladder or asks an emulation to state which one it reaches, and adoption of the label is not accompanied by adoption of the components it names.

resolving_work.title: Target trial emulation studies in oncology: a comprehensive analysis
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Documents how widely the label is applied in one specialty and how variably the underlying design is executed.

resolving_work.title: Reporting of observational studies explicitly aiming to emulate randomized trials: a systematic review
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Quantifies the gap between claiming the framework and reporting its components.

opinions.rationale: The variance problem for the sequence-expansion half of this entry has been addressed: a 2025 paper compares sandwich, nonparametric bootstrap, jackknife and linearized estimating function bootstrap confidence intervals for sequential trial emulation with survival outcomes and finds a computationally feasible option with better coverage in the motivating regime. The entry should not present that as open. The cloning half is not covered by that work, and a search for variance estimation under cloning specifically returned nothing, so the dependence induced by copies of the same person remains unaddressed. The computational directions the entry proposes, streaming risk sets and columnar back ends, appear nowhere in the corpus.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: Variance estimation for sequence expansion has been studied and a feasible recommendation exists; variance under cloning, where several rows are copies of one person's history, has not been addressed, and no scalable implementation strategy is published.

resolving_work.title: Inference procedures in sequential trial emulation with survival outcomes
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Supplies and evaluates variance estimation for sequence expansion, including a bootstrap alternative fast enough to run.

opinions.rationale: The corpus contains synthetic patient generation aimed at causal effect estimation and generative approaches to causal graphs, and contains no evaluation of a generative model against a known structural model's interventional distributions. The entry's claim, that fidelity evaluation does not test causal validity, is consistent with the absence, and the confidence is capped because the generative-model literature sits mostly in venues these eight phrases would not retrieve.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: Generative patient models are evaluated on distributional fidelity rather than against known interventional distributions, and no benchmark supplies a gold-standard structural model with counterfactuals to score them.

resolving_work.title: Generating high-fidelity privacy-conscious synthetic patient data for causal effect estimation with multiple treatments
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Targets synthetic generation at causal estimation, which is where the fidelity question becomes consequential.

opinions.rationale: The corpus contains reporting standards, quality assessment tools and comprehensive analyses of emulation practice, and none requires or reports the release of analysis code, complete phenotype logic with code-set versions, weight diagnostics or simulated test data. The automated-code-generation paper implies the artifacts exist in machine-readable form, which strengthens the entry: the material could be released and is not.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: No reporting standard or appraisal instrument for emulations requires release of analysis code, phenotype logic with code-set versions, weight diagnostics or simulated test data, and published emulations do not supply them.

resolving_work.title: From study design to executable code: automating target trial emulation with large language models
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Produces the executable specification as an artifact, which shows the material a reproducibility requirement would ask for is producible.

opinions.rationale: Automated translation from study design to executable emulation code exists, and agentic authoring of OMOP concept sets from natural language is now being attempted, so the systems the entry describes are real and multiplying. Nothing in the corpus supplies the validation regime the entry asks for: no typed intermediate representation, no temporal-logic validation, no synthetic test patients constructed to distinguish the correct reading of a temporal condition from the plausible wrong one, and no dual sign-off requirement. The gap between capability and validation is the claim, and the corpus shows only the capability half.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: Systems that translate study designs into executable cohort and analysis code exist and are being extended to concept-set authoring; no validation regime treats their output as untrusted, and temporal-logic errors that change the estimand would not be caught.

resolving_work.title: From study design to executable code: automating target trial emulation with large language models
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Builds the translation the entry is concerned about, which establishes the capability without supplying the validation.

resolving_work.title: Agentic authoring of OMOP concept sets from natural language
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Extends automation to phenotype definition, which is the component where a silent error changes the cohort.

opinions.rationale: A search for treatment leakage, temporal locking or auditing of learned representations used as adjustment sets returned nothing in the screened corpus. The claim is therefore unrefuted and weakly evidenced: the corpus is built from target trial and g-method phrases, and work on representation leakage would most likely appear in machine learning venues that none of the eight phrases reaches. The vote is open at the confidence ceiling this project sets for searched-and-found-nothing.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: No published emulation audits a text-derived representation used for adjustment for post-treatment information, and no convention states what window of text an encoder was permitted to see.

opinions.rationale: Subgroup estimation inside emulations is being done carefully in places the entry does not credit. A 2026 European Journal of Epidemiology paper extends a CONFIRM emulation to subgroups explicitly, a 2026 Alzheimer's and Dementia paper estimates heterogeneous statin effects on dementia with causal machine learning inside an emulation, and a 2026 Epidemiology paper nests a target study within a target trial specifically to evaluate intervention effects on disparities, which is the equity question the entry raises. What remains is the reporting requirement: none of these establishes that subgroup-specific data support and calibration must be reported alongside every subgroup effect, and none tests whether the emulation's assumptions differ across groups.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: Subgroup and heterogeneous-effect estimation within emulations is developing, including a framework aimed at disparities; no requirement exists to report subgroup-specific overlap and calibration, or to test whether identification assumptions hold equally across groups.

resolving_work.title: Nesting a target study within a target trial: a framework for evaluating intervention effects on disparities
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Provides a framework for the equity question the entry raises, within the emulation setting.

resolving_work.title: A target trial emulation of the CONFIRM study with an extension to subgroups
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: A worked subgroup extension of an emulation, showing the practice exists.

resolving_work.title: The heterogeneous treatment effects of statins on dementia: a target trial emulation with causal machine learning
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Applies causal machine learning for heterogeneity inside an emulation, which is the combination the entry describes as hazardous.

opinions.rationale: The corpus contains a growing body of flexible estimation inside emulations, including ensemble-learning marginal structural models and deep learning comparisons, and it contains no support diagnostic reported alongside a flexible nuisance model and no methods comparison that includes a deliberately non-identifiable scenario. A 2026 Nature Communications paper evaluates bias across statistical and deep learning methods in a heart failure emulation, which is the comparison the entry wants and does not include a non-identifiable arm. Failure awareness as a scored property does not appear anywhere.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: Flexible estimators are applied within emulations without an accompanying support diagnostic, and no published methods comparison scores whether an estimator's diagnostics correctly signal a non-identifiable target.

resolving_work.title: Evaluating bias in target trial emulation for heart failure across statistical and deep learning methods
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Compares flexible against conventional estimation for bias inside an emulation, which is the nearest existing test and does not include a non-identifiable scenario.

resolving_work.title: Estimate time-varying exposure effects via ensemble learning-based marginal structural model
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Applies ensemble learning to the weight model in a longitudinal setting, which is where the extrapolation concern applies.
